featured_reviews.review_text:
If you're looking for a place to learn swimming, I would highly recommend Rose Delight. This is more like a community driven project. There’s a real "family vibe" here that puts you at ease the moment you walk in.

The trainers—Paul, Daniel and the larger team—are fantastic. They have a massive amount of patience and a clear love for what they do, especially when it comes to teaching kids.

I have personally seen my 7yo son go step by step and learn swimming in just a few sessions.

Paul and team really take huge efforts and patience to train the technical stuff like breathing, floating, and building up stamina so you don't get tired out.

It’s a great spot for both adults and children to learn. It’s rare to find a place that cares this much about the people they are teaching. If you want to learn swimming in a supportive, loving, and professional setting, this is the perfect place to dive in! 🏊🏼‍♂️

featured_reviews.name: Sandesh Padyar
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is a well-developed infrastructure project by the VVMC. Inaugurated in 2009, the pool has been operational regularly for the last 17 years (except during the COVID-19 pandemic), which is highly commendable. If you want to pursue swimming as a hobby at an affordable rate of just 500 INR per month, this is a great choice.
​Pros:
​Olympic Size: Because it is built to Olympic standards, it easily handles a crowd of 70 to 80 members per batch without feeling overly congested.
​Water Upkeep: Water cleanliness issues arise occasionally, but the management is generally quick to address and resolve them.
​Cons & Areas for Improvement:
​Staff Management: Except for 2 or 3 efficient lifeguards, the rest of the staff is quite passive. They also tend to rush members out, closing the batch 10 minutes prior to the official end time.
​Changing Room Maintenance: The facility lacks basic amenities. The locker system has been discontinued, there are no racks to store bags, and there aren't enough benches to sit on while changing.
​Plumbing & Safety: The shower taps and fittings are in poor condition. Additionally, there are no anti-skid mats installed in the changing or shower areas, making them slippery and unsafe.
​Verdict: An excellent budget-friendly Olympic-sized facility for local residents, provided you can overlook the average upkeep of the changing rooms.

featured_reviews.review_text: Ameya Classic Club in Virar West is a fantastic place to unwind and enjoy a variety of activities. featured_reviews.name: Soniii
featured_reviews.review_text:
Throwback to one of the most vibrant Holi celebrations of this year — Yashwant Nagar, Virar West (at Ameya Club)!
Still can’t get over the colors, the energy, and the non-stop fun. The DJ was full josh, rain dance setup was on point, and the atmosphere was pure madness — laughter, dance, and total enjoyment!

The food stole the show, especially the chole bhature — piping hot, delicious, and perfect for the festive mood. And yes, the bhang just hit different!

There were desi-style games, trampolines, and a full family vibe all around. Crowd was super lively, and both online/offline bookings were handled really well.

The lucky draw at the end was a surprise treat — amazing prizes and total excitement! For a first-time event, the team seriously nailed it.

Also, a shoutout to Ameya Club — the venue was just perfect! With facilities like skating, swimming pool, and open spaces for everything from weddings to sports events, it's a great spot for any big celebration. If you're planning any function, this place has it all!

featured_reviews.name: swapnil patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
Praful, who introduced himself as the operations manager at the swimming area, behaved extremely rudely when my wife rushed to save our child, who started struggling in the water after another boy’s floater hit his face while swimming. Shockingly, there was no lifeguard or swimming coach present at that moment.

Instead of helping or showing concern for our child’s safety, Praful was more worried about footwear touching the pool wall. As parents, our only priority was saving my child. When I pointed out the absence of staff and mentioned that I was already aware of previous safety-related incidents and concerns at the pool, Praful arrogantly replied that I should not have taken admission if I was aware of the history. Praful also made an insensitive remark to the swimming staff saying, “Hyanna watata lifeguard ne fakt hichya poravar laksha dyayacha.”

If this is the behaviour and attitude of a person in charge of operations, it is difficult to expect professionalism, sensitivity, or responsibility from the ground staff.

Praful’s insensitive and irresponsible behaviour is the reason I am withdrawing from the swimming session..

featured_reviews.name: Kushal Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
There was a time when this gym was one of the best in town, but it has degraded quite a lot. While the trainers remain nice, the management's performance has declined day by day. For instance, one corner of the ceiling has been exposed and left untreated for several months. They attribute this leakage to illegal restrooms being constructed by tenants above them, a situation that seems to involve complex building politics. However, setting aside the underlying issues, the aesthetic and cleanliness concerns are immediately apparent.

Furthermore, the gym frequently experiences significant electricity issues. This often results in no lights or fans, let alone air conditioning. Although they have an inverter backup, it only lasts for a brief 15-20 minutes. After that, members are left to work out with no fan, no light, and minimal ventilation from the windows. This is not only a health hazard but also makes effective workouts nearly impossible. This problem has been recurring for 1-2 days every month for the past couple of months, yet management has shown no initiative to fix the inverter battery. When higher management was contacted, they simply claimed that "things take time," and "everyone wants all things at a budget price." Disturbingly, they later suggested, "if you are not comfortable you can leave the gym at will and don’t disturb by contacting us."

The comfort factor has indeed been absent from the gym for a long time. As much as I once loved this gym, its current condition is the worst. Management seems to neither understand nor imagine how difficult it is to work out without fans or proper ventilation during these power cuts. No one is asking for generators or constant AC during outages, but functional fans are essential. It would be understandable if the fans worked for a few hours after a power cut, but 15 minutes is simply inadequate. There's a clear lack of understanding regarding members' concerns and no visible steps towards improvement. Members who have paid for their entire membership are now suffering due to these persistent issues.

It's truly disheartening that they are setting a precedent by telling members to leave if they are not comfortable, effectively saying, "this is how it is, and you can leave at your will." Instead, why not focus on improving the facilities and restoring the gym to its former standard? Such statements from upper management were genuinely surprising and disappointing. As much as this gym played a role in getting me into becomming fit with dedication, hardwork along with the help of trainers, sirs, and equipment, it is sad to see it transistioned into this because of mismanagement.

featured_reviews.name: Drishti_Capital
featured_reviews.review_text:
Honest Review About the Gym

I am writing this review to share an honest experience so that management can improve their services.

Recently, my friend joined this gym and paid for an annual membership along with one month of personal training. Unfortunately, she did not receive proper personal training service. The first trainer assigned to her did not train her properly and then left the gym. After that, a second trainer was assigned, and he also left the gym. Because of this, she did not get the full one-month personal training service as promised. This was disappointing.

In the last two months, many trainers have left the gym. Now there are mostly new faces. This makes us feel that the environment for trainers may not be stable, and this affects members as well.

Another important point is about guidance during workouts. My friend and I were sometimes doing exercises with the wrong form. The trainer saw us but did not correct us. Later, some other members helped us with the correct form. It is the moral responsibility of trainers to guide members when they see someone doing an exercise incorrectly, as wrong form can lead to injury.

We understand that trainers focus more on personal training because it is their main source of extra income. However, when a trainer is standing idle and clearly sees someone performing an exercise incorrectly that could cause injury, it is important to step in and guide them. Basic safety guidance should not depend on whether someone has taken personal training or not. Ignoring such situations is disappointing and unsafe.

We were also informed that the gym has around 3000 registered members. If even 2000 members come daily and there are only around 7 trainers, that means each trainer would have to observe around 250–300 members. This makes it very difficult to give proper attention to everyone.

We have also noticed that many trainers spend time at the back side instead of actively guiding members on the floor.

On the positive side, the gym has all the necessary equipment required for workouts. The gym also offers activities like Yoga, Zumba, Kickboxing, and organizes events like badminton games, Garba, and annual celebrations. The gym area is large (around 10,000 sq. ft.), and the overall environment and vibes are good.

However, for new members, proper guidance in the initial phase is more important than just equipment or space.

Also, every hard-earned money paid as membership fees should be valued properly. When members pay for services, they expect quality service in return. The gym should ensure that members receive the best possible service according to what they have paid for.

This review is not written to blame the gym but to give honest feedback to management. We hope management will take corrective actions and improve trainer stability and member guidance to maintain the gym’s brand image.

Thank you.

Extremely Disappointed - one star is also too much to give.

I have a severe lower back injury due to extremely irresponsible training at this gym. The trainer, who is also the owner (Mukesh sir), forced me to lift a 100kg deadlift despite my hesitation and lack of proper guidance. As a result, I suffered a disc bulge that has not healed even after a year of ongoing treatment.

I'm a professional Kabaddi Athlete and because of this injury, I can’t even play my sport anymore. This injury has impacted every part of my life – sitting, walking, sleeping – everything hurts.

What’s worse is that months later, when I returned to the gym for light rehab, Mukesh sir again advised me to do deadlifts, claiming it would help recovery – which is medically irrational and highly risky.

This experience has made me lose valuable time in my athletic career, affected my physical and mental health, and cost me emotionally and financially.

I strongly do NOT recommend this gym and advise others – especially athletes or beginners – to avoid this gym. especially training under Mukesh sir. He pushes clients beyond their limits without proper consent and understanding, and clearly lacks the expertise and knowledge needed to train safely.

There are better, more professional gyms nearby with certified trainers - please prioritize your health and safety.
